sources: TUESDAY Oct 20 2026 EARLY RUN (06:20 UTC, before the US open). US cash closes are MONDAY Oct 19; oil, metals and FX carry live Tuesday European-session quotes. HEADLINE 1 - THE OIL RELIEF LASTED ONE DAY. Brent is back to 110.85 USD/Bbl (plus 1.1 to 1.2 pct on the day, TradingEconomics Oct 20 serving 110.76-110.85), erasing Monday's sanctions-waiver dip to 107.86 and printing a NEW HIGH for this episode above the Oct 16 intraday 110 touch. Fresh attacks on Gulf shipping and refineries are outweighing the Russian sanctions waiver and the Iranian Hormuz reopening offer. The waiver and the Hormuz offer are both still on the table, so the bullish and bearish forces are now stacked against each other at a higher price, which is the worst configuration for volatility. Brent is roughly 33 pct above pre-war levels. Trend up, and this is the single most important tile on the board. HEADLINE 2 - THE VIX SPIKE WAS SMALLER THAN WE REPORTED AND IT HAS ALREADY REVERSED. FRED VIXCLS finally posted Oct 16 at 19.99, NOT the 21.41 wire value this dashboard carried for four runs - 21.41 was the Friday INTRADAY HIGH (darktrader confirms Friday intraday high 22.31, close 19.99), so the previous four runs overstated equity vol by about 1.4 points. Correction applied. Monday Oct 19 then closed at 18.07, down 1.92 or minus 9.6 pct, as AI and chip names rebounded (S and P 500 plus 50 to 7,709.63, Nasdaq plus 1.1 pct to 26,430.89, Dow minus slightly, Russell plus 7). So the official path is 15.27 Oct 13, 16.87 Oct 14, 16.46 Oct 15, 19.99 Oct 16, 18.07 Oct 19. Equity vol is still up about 18 pct on the week but it is falling, not rising, and it never reached the panic level the board was showing. NOTE ONE UNRESOLVED DISCREPANCY: Yahoo/AOL report the Oct 19 VIX close as 18.44 (minus 1.55) while ad-hoc-news reports 18.07 (minus 1.92, minus 9.6 pct) and darktrader has 18.15 intraday (minus 9.2 pct). The 18.07 figure is used here because it is explicitly a close and reconciles exactly with the FRED Oct 16 print of 19.99. True value is almost certainly 18.0 to 18.5. FRED will confirm Oct 19 later today. RATES AND CREDIT: the curve steepened slightly. 10Y 5.071 pct Oct 19 (5.098 Oct 16, 5.087 Oct 15, 5.190 Oct 14, 5.217 Oct 13) and 2Y 4.708 pct, giving a 2s10s of about 0.36 versus the FRED T10Y2Y Oct 16 print of 0.35 (0.33 Oct 15, 0.37 Oct 14, 0.42 Oct 13). So the curve is still at the flat end of this episode, down about 6bp on the week, but it has stopped flattening and the whole 10Y curve has rallied about 13bp in a week - bonds are being bought, not sold, which argues against an inflation-panic read of the oil move. FRED T5YIFR Oct 16 2.33 (2.31, 2.34, 2.33) - 5y5y breakevens are FLAT ON THE WEEK for a fifth run despite Brent at a new episode high. This remains the single most reassuring number on the board. FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 is STILL stuck at Oct 15 3.23 pct (3.25 Oct 14, 3.16 Oct 13, 3.11 Oct 12, 3.11 Oct 9) - FRED has now failed to post Oct 16 for a second day, so the Friday rout is STILL not in the credit data and 323bp is carried. TradingEconomics serves a monthly October figure of 3.25 pct, which is consistent. Credit is out of its 303-312 band to the wide side, plus 12bp on the week, and the post-rout print is the most important missing number on this board. FINANCIAL CONDITIONS AND LABOUR - BOTH CARRIED, BOTH STALE: FRED NFCI week ending Oct 9 minus 0.499 (minus 0.507, minus 0.517, minus 0.527, minus 0.536) - a fifth week of drift tighter from a very loose base, and it still pre-dates the selloff; the first post-selloff read lands TOMORROW Oct 21. FRED ICSA week ending Oct 10 199k (198k Oct 3, 199k Sep 26, 198k Sep 19, 198k Sep 12) - fifth straight week in a 198-199k range, next release Oct 22. Labour remains the strongest tile on the board and the claims trend is reclassified from up to FLAT, since 199 versus 198 is noise. DOLLAR AND GROWTH PROXY: DXY 101.93 (plus 0.09 pct, previous close 101.84; FXStreet has it near 101.80 in early European trade, so call it 101.8-101.9) - down about 0.25 pct on the week and STILL refusing to rally on a new oil high and a hawkish CPI. A dollar that will not bid in a supply shock remains the odd one out on this board. Growth proxy 1.59, up from four consecutive runs at 1.57 (copper 6.54 USD/Lbs roughly flat at plus 0.03 pct, gold 4,124.02 USD/t.oz minus 0.41 pct and now DOWN THREE STRAIGHT DAYS from 4,181, having repeatedly failed above 4,200; 6.54/4124.02*1000 = 1.586). The ratio is rising because gold is selling off, not because copper is rallying, which is a mild risk-on signal and the opposite of a growth scare. Trend kept FLAT - a 1.3 pct move does not earn an arrow. REAL ECONOMY - ALL CARRIED: consumer sentiment 46.3 (UMich preliminary October, five-month low, one-year inflation expectations 4.7 pct and five-year 3.5 pct) trend down; ISM Manufacturing 54.5 (September, next Nov 2); building permits 1,403k (August) - the SEPTEMBER release lands TODAY Oct 20 at 12:30 UTC, which is AFTER this run, so it will be picked up tomorrow; LEI y/y minus 0.7 pct (September release Oct 22); Sahm Rule 0.00 (September, next Nov 6, trigger plus 0.50). All flat. MONETARY PLUMBING - STILL BLIND, FIFTH RUN: the 3M SOFR-OIS spread was searched again (traditiondata, bluegamma, sofrrate, sofracademy, cbonds, global-rates) and every free source serves the SOFR level or an OIS rate, never the spread, so 0bp is CARRIED AS A STANDING ASSUMPTION, NOT A MEASUREMENT. The EUR/USD 3M cross-currency basis is also CARRIED AS AN ASSUMPTION at minus 10bp - no free source publishes it. Global liquidity 1 (stable) is a judgement call: no balance-sheet regime change was found for the Fed, ECB, PBOC or BOJ this run. Two assumed tiles and one judgement tile out of eighteen, unchanged for a fifth run. FED: Oct 27-28 FOMC, fed funds target 3.75-4.00 pct, hold remains the heavy consensus; no new pricing found this run, so the roughly 85 pct hold from Oct 19 stands. INFRASTRUCTURE: git healthy, working tree clean at start, no stale locks, this scheduled session remains the sole writer of data.json (GitHub Action disabled since Oct 17), BDTI stayed removed. STILL OPEN - SECURITY, FIFTH RUN: the origin remote is an HTTPS URL with a GitHub personal access token in plain text in .git/config. Fine-grained and repo-scoped, but it should be rotated and replaced with an SSH remote. Also still present: untracked junk in the repo root - _stale_git_locks/, _wtest, __pycache__/ and outputs/ - all safe to delete. PICTURE: the board has split cleanly in two overnight. The FINANCIAL side is healing - equity vol down 10 pct and revealed to have been overstated, the curve steepening, the 10Y rallying 13bp on the week, breakevens flat at 2.33, gold selling off, claims below 200k for a fifth week, and stocks bouncing on the AI names that caused the rout. The PHYSICAL side is deteriorating - Brent at a new episode high above 110 with attacks on Gulf shipping overwhelming two separate pieces of bullish-for-supply news. That combination is unusual and it is informative: the market is treating this as an energy supply shock, not a systemic or recessionary event. The honest read is an AI-valuation wobble that is already mean-reverting, sitting on top of a live and worsening oil shock that the bond market has so far declined to price as inflationary. The two genuine risks are that the missing HY OAS print lands wide, and that oil keeps going. WATCH, IN ORDER OF WEIGHT: whether Brent holds above 110 or the Hormuz reopening is actually accepted; whether FRED finally posts Oct 16 and Oct 19 HY OAS and where it lands; NFCI TOMORROW Oct 21 for the first post-selloff financial conditions read; September building permits TODAY Oct 20 12:30 UTC; claims and September LEI Oct 22; EIA inventories Oct 21; the Oct 27-28 FOMC; whether FRED confirms the Oct 19 VIX near 18.07 or nearer 18.44; rotating the embedded PAT.
